claim_text: Quantum cryptography exploits quantum-mechanical properties such as quantum entanglement, measurement disturbance, the no-cloning theorem, and superposition to perform encryption tasks.
Quantum encryption plays a crucial role in the secure processing, storage, and transmission of information.
Sufficiently powerful quantum computers can break widely used encryption systems including RSA, elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), and Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
Quantum computers can break RSA and ECC encryption, compromising secure communications, authentication, and data integrity.
The quantum threat poses an existential threat to the encryption algorithms that protect everything from personal communications to national security secrets.
Quantum computers breaking RSA and ECC threatens the security of government, enterprise, and critical infrastructure.
